rationale: Build on the best 9x512 recurrent-tail script by making the repeated tail blocks behave more like refinement passes than exact replays. This adds a tiny learned per-head multiplier that only applies to the recurrent tail attention pass, initialized below 1.0 so the second pass starts slightly softer while the first pass and all non-tail blocks stay unchanged. The change is compile-stable, costs almost no bytes, preserves the proven quant-aware endgame and FP16 tail rescue, and directly targets the underexplored recurrence-scheduling behavior that still looks more promising here than another small optimizer sweep.
title: Recurrent-Pass Tail Attention Softening
